explicitmemory.short: History stored outside the model in an inspectable form such as a transcript, summary, or structured state.
explicitmemory.long: H1 begins with explicit memory because it is a strong, simple control. If ordinary written history already solves a problem, hidden recurrence should not receive credit for solving it.

structuredstate.short: The typed Level-1 state object used to store working memory, goals, source information, and unresolved items.
structuredstate.long: StructuredSelfState is not assumed to be a mind or self. It is an experimentally convenient control surface: bounded, inspectable, versioned, and easy to intervene on.

persistence.short: The property that a later state depends on an earlier state rather than every episode starting from scratch.
persistence.long: H1 studies scaffolded persistence: state is explicitly carried across ticks. S06 shows that deterministic Level-1 state can also be reconstructed later from the event history.

recurrence.short: A system whose internal state is repeatedly fed forward to influence later processing.
recurrence.long: The project reserves the stronger recurrence question for H2, where hidden state itself is carried and causally manipulated. H1 is an explicit-memory control, not yet genuine latent recurrence.

latentstate.short: A hidden internal representation carried by the model rather than a visible text or JSON record.
latentstate.long: H2 will ask whether native hidden state carries causal history that cannot be reduced to rereading or deterministically reconstructing an external record.

transcript.short: The raw chronological history of events given directly to the model at evaluation time.
transcript.long: The transcript is an important control because it preserves the whole observable history. In S06, raw transcript access was not resolved as less accurate than scheduled structured state.

detreplay.short: Rebuilding the same explicit state later by applying the same deterministic update rules to the same ordered event history.
detreplay.long: If online processing and deterministic replay end in the identical state and prompt, then scheduling those explicit transitions through time did not create a unique final representation.

modelrecon.short: Asking the language model itself to compress the full history into the structured state in one retrospective pass.
modelrecon.long: This differs from deterministic replay. In final E05d, Qwen2.5-3B validated a real reconstructed state but still performed substantially worse than the deterministically maintained state.

nulltick.short: A processing interval with no new task-relevant external information.
nulltick.long: S07 asks whether meaningful state changes can happen during such intervals. A null tick can include computation; it simply may not introduce new semantic evidence about the task.

quiettick.short: In S05, a tick with no incoming event that was implemented as a deterministic identity no-op.
quiettick.long: Quiet-tick stability showed that the scaffold could remain stable. It did not show autonomous hidden cognition, because the model was not called during these identity ticks.

oracle.short: A rule-based state updater used as the reliable Level-1 control substrate.
oracle.long: The updater deterministically maps events into StructuredSelfState. It is intentionally stronger and more reliable than the tested Qwen2.5-3B autonomous update procedures.

delta.short: Updating only what changed instead of rewriting the entire state.
delta.long: In S05, delta updating was less destructive than full-state rewriting, but Qwen2.5-3B still omitted most state and was not reliable enough to become the canonical maintainer.

errorinheritance.short: Persistence can preserve a false state just as effectively as a true one.
errorinheritance.long: S05 showed why memory is not automatically intelligence. Once a bad update is written into a persistent state, the architecture can protect that error over time.

forcedchoice.short: A task where the model selects from a fixed set of candidate answers.
forcedchoice.long: Forced-choice probes reduce exact-generation burden. H1 later hardened the candidates so all options appeared in context, preventing simple familiarity from solving the task.

incontextfoils.short: Incorrect answer options that really appeared elsewhere in the same episode.
incontextfoils.long: This prevents a model from answering merely by selecting the only candidate it remembers seeing. It must retrieve the correct binding or follow the actual relation.

bootstrap.short: A resampling method that treats whole episodes as the unit of resampling.
bootstrap.long: Multiple probes from one episode are correlated. Resampling episodes rather than individual trials better reflects that dependency when estimating uncertainty.

mcnemar.short: A paired test that focuses on items where two conditions disagree.
mcnemar.long: H1 uses exact two-sided binomial McNemar tests as supplementary trial-level inference.

permutation.short: A cluster-level paired test asking whether episode-level differences could plausibly arise if their signs were exchangeable.
permutation.long: The final S06 reporting treats the episode-level sign-flip test as the primary inferential decision criterion, with bootstrap intervals showing effect-size uncertainty.

chance.short: Expected accuracy when choosing randomly among the offered answers.
chance.long: The H1 battery mixes three 4-choice probes and one 3-choice probe, giving a nominal average chance level of about 27.1%.

claimceiling.short: The strongest conclusion the current evidence is allowed to support.
claimceiling.long: A useful result can still have a low claim ceiling. H1 can support engineering and behavioral claims about explicit state without supporting claims about phenomenal consciousness or irreducible selfhood.
